U0100.d: U0100 is stored by a module that has stopped hearing the engine or powertrain controller, ECM/PCM A; a second engine controller has its own code, U0115. Usually the transmission controller logs it, often alongside other listeners.
s: MIL on, often several U codes in other modules
Transmission stuck in a substitute gear or harsh shifts
Gauges for engine speed or temperature drop out
Engine may stall or not crank
c: ECM/PCM without power or ground (fuse, main relay, ground point)
Damaged CAN lines or loose, corroded terminals between ECM and TCM
Weak battery or voltage dip during cranking (history code)
ECM internally faulty or software not running

U0101.d: U0101 means the transmission controller has dropped off the bus as seen by another node, mostly the engine controller. GM's 2019 truck ECMs watch eight TCM frames, most of them at 500 ms intervals, and set the code as Type A after battery and run voltage have exceeded 11 V for 3 s, provided U0073 is not active; GM's electronic range selector logs it as Type B after 1 s, the hybrid processor in the same table after 5
s: MIL on, transmission warning in the cluster
Gear indicator blank or flashing
Transmission locked in one gear
Scan tool cannot reach the TCM
c: TCM without power or ground (fuse, relay, connector)
Spread or corroded terminals at the transmission harness connector
Chafed or open CAN lines to the TCM
TCM internally faulty, overheated or not programmed

U0102.d: U0102 is logged when the transfer case control module, which shifts between two- and four-wheel drive and between high and low range, stops sending. GM's 2025 engine controllers expect frame $035 and fail it when gaps exceed 425 ms within a 5 s window; the code is Type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL.
s: 4WD or AWD warning, range selection ignored
Transfer case stays in its last mode
Usually no MIL
c: Transfer case module without power or ground
Water or corrosion in the module connector (often mounted low on the frame)
Damaged CAN lines to the transfer case module

U0103.d: U0103 points to gear shift control module A, the electronic selector (lever, rotary knob or buttons) in shift-by-wire cars. GM's 2025 engine controllers talk to it over a LIN line and set the code as Type B once its response is absent for at least 500 ms.
s: Service Shifter or Shift System Fault message
Selector stuck in Park or gear changes refused
MIL or wrench lamp on
Intermittent no-crank
c: Selector module software fault (update available from the maker)
Loose ground or blown fuse feeding the selector
Open or shorted LIN/CAN line to the selector

U0104.d: U0104 names the cruise control module, today usually the radar unit of adaptive cruise control that sends speed and distance requests to the engine. GM's 2019 truck ECMs check its frames $2CB and $2CD, treat gaps beyond 500 ms that persist for 3 s as a failure and classify the result as Type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL; detection pauses while the bus-off code of the carrying bus (U0073, U0074) is active.
s: Cruise or adaptive cruise unavailable, warning message
Forward collision alert may switch off as well
No MIL
c: Radar/cruise module without power or with a wet, loose connector (front bumper area)
Front-end damage or bumper repair affecting module or wiring
Damaged CAN lines to the module

U0105.d: U0105 concerns a separate fuel injector control module that drives the injectors on command of the engine controller. GM's 2005 Duramax 6.6 L (LLY) received a status message from this injector driver via CAN (J1939) whose toggle bit must flip every 20 ms; if it stalls for three updates, 30 failures in 50 checks give a Type B code.
s: MIL on
Misfire, rough running or reduced power
Engine stalls or will not start
c: Injector module supply low or missing (fuse, relay, battery voltage)
Loose or corroded connector or damaged CAN lines to the module
Injector module internally faulty (heat, power stage)

U0106.d: U0106 reports that glow plug control module 1 of a diesel engine no longer communicates. In Ford's 2023 diesel summary (6.7 L and 3.0 L) the GPCM is declared lost after 5 s of silence.
s: MIL on
Long cranking or no start when cold
White smoke after cold start
Wait-to-start lamp behaves oddly
c: Water or corrosion in the glow plug module connector or harness
Module supply fuse, relay or ground faulty
Damaged CAN lines to the glow plug module
Glow plug module internally faulty (overtemperature, driver)

U0107.d: U0107 targets a stand-alone throttle actuator control (TAC) module, as used before throttle control moved into the engine controller. In GM's 2004 and 2005 truck tables (4.3–6.0 L and 8.1 L) the PCM and TAC module traded data over a dedicated serial link; the PCM declared a gap after 18.75 ms and the TAC module after 25 ms.
s: MIL on
Reduced engine power, throttle barely opens
Idle unstable or engine stalls
c: Open, shorted or chafed serial data lines between PCM and TAC module
TAC module supply or ground faulty
Corroded connector at the TAC module

U0108.d: U0108 covers a separate controller for an alternative fuel such as LPG or CNG, added to an engine that otherwise runs a gasoline control strategy. Roush CleanTech's fourth-generation propane systems for Ford E- and F-Series trucks (2016–2018) are a documented user: the PCM expects CAN traffic from the system's Smart Relay Module and stores U0108 when those messages keep missing.
s: MIL on
Rough idle or poor running on the alternative fuel
System may stay on or revert to gasoline
c: Alternative fuel module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Damaged CAN wiring between conversion module and PCM
Water or corrosion in the module connectors

U0109.d: U0109 means the engine controller no longer hears fuel pump control module A, the electronics that drive the in-tank pump at variable speed. GM's 2019 Corvette LT5 table watches frames $1EB and $4D9 and sets the code after 10 s as Type B over two trips.
s: MIL on
Long cranking, stalling or no start
Hesitation under load from low fuel pressure
c: Loose fuse, relay or feed terminal supplying the pump module
Fuel pump module internally faulty (common on some trucks, replaced by bulletin)
Corroded connector or damaged wiring near the tank or frame
Engine controller software setting the code falsely

U010A.d: U010A is set when a stand-alone control module for exhaust gas recirculation A stops communicating. J2012 reserves this slot for engines whose EGR valve or EGR system is run by its own electronics on the bus rather than as a plain output of the engine controller; module B (U010B) would be a second such unit.
s: MIL on
EGR deactivated, higher NOx
Possible reduced power mode
c: EGR module A without power or ground
Heat-damaged wiring or connector near the exhaust side
Open or shorted bus lines to module A

U010B.d: U010B names the second exhaust gas recirculation control module, B. Its existence implies an engine with two separately controlled EGR units, for example a high- and a low-pressure loop on a diesel or one unit per cylinder bank; which one is B is the maker's choice.
s: MIL on
Second EGR path inactive, possible NOx increase
Module B not reachable with a scan tool
c: EGR module B without power or ground
Open or chafed bus branch to module B
Loose or heat-damaged connector at module B

U010C.d: U010C reports that turbocharger/supercharger control module A, in practice the electronic actuator that positions variable-geometry vanes or a wastegate, has gone silent. GM's 2017 small-diesel table (2.8 L Duramax and Cruze diesel) watches its frames $099 and $499 on a dedicated sensor bus and logs U010C once 10 s pass without them, rated Type B with two trips, provided that bus is not off (U0076).
s: MIL on
Low power, reduced boost
Other boost codes such as P003A or P0234 stored
c: Electronic turbo actuator faulty (heat, internal electronics)
Actuator supply, fuse or ground faulty
Heat-damaged connector or bus lines at the turbo

U010D.d: U010D is the counterpart of U010C for a second charger control module, B. It applies to engines with two independently actuated chargers, such as sequential or twin turbo layouts, or a turbo plus an electronically controlled supercharger.
s: MIL on
Reduced power, second charger not used
Module B not reachable with a scan tool
c: Charger module B without power or ground
Heat-damaged wiring or connector at the second charger

U010E.d: U010E concerns the reductant control module that runs dosing, pump and heaters of a diesel SCR system with urea solution (DEF/AdBlue). GM's 2017 small-diesel table expects frame $092 and several $4Cx/$4Ex frames on bus B and, after 10 s of silence, records a Type A fault with MIL on the first trip, unless bus B is off (U0074).
s: MIL and DEF/AdBlue warning
Countdown to speed limit or restart block
Further SCR codes such as P20EE
c: Reductant module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Corroded or wet connector at the tank-mounted module
Damaged bus lines along the frame to the module
Engine controller software setting the code falsely

U010F.d: U010F is logged when the air conditioning control module stops reporting. J2012 keeps it apart from the HVAC control module (U0164): the A/C unit governs the refrigerant side, such as compressor clutch or electric compressor drive and pressures, while the HVAC module handles blower, flaps and temperature choice.
s: Air conditioning does not cool
Windows fog up, demisting weak
No MIL
c: A/C module without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Damaged bus lines to the A/C module
Condensate or water at module or connector

U0110.d: U0110 means drive motor control module A, the power electronics running the electric traction motor of a hybrid or EV, has stopped talking. Audi's TSB 2065538/1 (Q5 and A7 PHEV, 2019–2021) finds U011000 in the transmission controller after a brief 12 V dip trips the low-voltage monitor; a full bus sleep of about 20 minutes plus clearing codes cures it.
s: Vehicle does not enter READY or will not start
Red drive-system or electrical warning
Electric drive unavailable, limp mode
c: 12 V battery weak or voltage dip, inverter electronics drop off the bus
Water or corrosion in high- or low-voltage connectors of the drive system
Damaged CAN lines to the inverter
Drive motor control module internally faulty

U0111.d: U0111 indicates that battery energy control module A, which measures cell voltages, temperatures and current of the high-voltage or 48 V battery, has dropped off the network. GM's 2018 Volt hybrid controller expects it on bus A and sets the code as Type B over two trips once messages have been absent for 5 s above 10.2 V; while it is pending, GM suspends pack voltage and current plausibility checks.
s: MIL or service-hybrid/charging warning
No READY, electric drive or charging unavailable
Start-stop inoperative (mild hybrid)
12 V battery drained
c: Battery module software or calibration fault (update released)
Module fails to wake up in extreme cold or after a 12 V dip
Damaged CAN lines or connector at the battery pack
Battery energy control module internally faulty

U0112.d: U0112 is logged when a second battery energy control module, B, stops talking on the bus while a partner still waits for its data. Mitsubishi's 2018 Outlander PHEV is a documented case: the main battery management unit (BMU) supervises a sub-BMU inside the traction pack and stores U0112 once that unit's frames have been missing for 0.3 s, after the BMU has seen 8–16 V for more than 2 s; the check follows drive-cycle
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric range or electric drive unavailable
Vehicle does not reach READY
c: Open, shorted or chafed CAN lines between main and sub battery module inside the pack
Corroded or loose connector at the traction battery
Battery module B internally faulty or without supply

U0113.d: Unlike its neighbours, U0113 does not name one unit but a class of data: messages a controller depends on for emission control, for instance torque, speed or aftertreatment status supplied by another node. CARB's OBD II rule wants silence from a digital input recognised as a fault of its own with a dedicated code, and U0113 is the generic slot for that situation.
s: MIL on
Engine on substitute values, possibly reduced power
Further U codes in other modules
c: Fault in the CAN wiring or connectors carrying the emission-related frames
Sending module without power, ground or wake-up
Software or configuration mismatch after module replacement or update

U0114.d: U0114 says the controller of a four-wheel-drive clutch has gone quiet. Such a unit sets how much torque reaches the secondary axle by clamping a multi-plate coupling, as in Haldex-type on-demand drivelines whose later generations carry their own integrated electronics.
s: AWD/4WD warning in the cluster
Drive only on the primary axle, wheelspin on slippery roads
Possibly stability control warning
c: Clutch module without power or ground (fuse, connector near the rear axle)
Water or corrosion in the module connector exposed under the car
Chafed or open CAN lines to the rear of the vehicle

U0115.d: U0115 is set when a second engine or powertrain controller, ECM/PCM B, vanishes from the bus; U0100 belongs to unit A. What B stands for depends on the maker: GM's Saab 9-5 and 9-4X lists call it ECM 2, Mercedes-Benz assigns U011500 to its drivetrain control unit.
s: MIL or engine/drive system warning
No start or no READY on hybrids
Often no driveability complaint when the code is software-related
c: Software fault in the reporting or the B controller (updates released)
Water ingress or corroded terminals on the bus or relay connectors
Controller B not powered or not woken up in time

U0116.d: U0116 means a module no longer hears the coolant temperature control module, a separate controller for engines with electronically managed cooling. Depending on the design it may command electric pumps, map-controlled valves or fans and pass coolant status on to the engine controller.
s: Engine temperature or cooling system warning
Cooling fan or electric pump running continuously
Reduced engine power as protection
c: Cooling module without power or ground (fuse, relay, ground point in the engine bay)
Heat-damaged or corroded connector near the engine
Damaged CAN or LIN wiring to the module
Coolant temperature control module internally faulty

U0117.d: U0117 points to a lost link with the power take-off (PTO) control module, which engages and governs an engine-driven output for auxiliary equipment such as a tipper body, aerial bucket or recovery winch. CARB defines such a PTO unit and lets the engine controller pause monitor counters while it runs, so dependable PTO status on the bus matters for OBD bookkeeping.
s: PTO cannot be engaged or disengages
Elevated idle or remote engine speed control unavailable
Warning message in the cluster
c: Faulty upfitter wiring or connector between chassis and PTO controller
PTO module without power or ground
Vehicle configuration expects a PTO module that is missing or not programmed

U0118.d: U0118 concerns the fuel additive control module, which on some diesel cars meters a fuel-borne catalyst from a separate tank into the fuel. The additive lowers the temperature at which trapped soot burns in the particulate filter from above 600 °C to roughly 350–450 °C.
s: MIL and particulate filter warning
Regeneration fails, filter loads up
Reduced power in later stages
c: Additive module unplugged or its fuse removed, e.g. after filter work
Corroded connector at the additive tank or module under the vehicle
Damaged CAN wiring to the additive module
Fuel additive control module internally faulty or not coded

U0119.d: U0119 is the slot for losing the fuel cell control module, the controller that runs the hydrogen stack of a fuel cell vehicle: air compressor, hydrogen supply, humidity, stack cooling and the electrical output handed to the drive. Older code tables still label U0116–U0120 as reserved, so some scan tools show no text for it.
s: Fuel cell or drive system warning
Power limited to the buffer battery
Vehicle does not reach READY
c: Fuel cell controller without 12 V supply or ground
Damaged CAN wiring or connector between stack controller and vehicle controller
Software fault or missing update in one of the controllers
Fuel cell control module internally faulty

U011A.d: U011A appears when the engine controller loses exhaust gas sensor module A, the electronics that heat and evaluate a wide-band oxygen probe (or a similar exhaust sensor) and send the result as bus data instead of analogue signals. Chrysler's bulletin 25-002-14, which replaces 25-003-13 and 25-004-13, lists it for 2010–2012 Ram 2500/3500 pickups with the 6.7 L Cummins among oxygen-sensor faults; the prescribed fix is
s: MIL on
Further oxygen-sensor codes stored
Particulate filter regeneration restricted
c: Heat-stressed wiring or poor terminal contact at the sensor module connector
Sensor module without power or ground
Exhaust gas sensor module internally faulty

U011B.d: U011B covers the first rocker arm control module. On overhead-cam engines that shut cylinders down or change valve lift, a solenoid routes engine oil to unhook a pin coupling two rocker arms; the cam-driven arm then moves on its own and the valve stays shut.
s: MIL on
Cylinder deactivation or valve lift switching inactive
Higher fuel consumption
c: Rocker arm module without power or ground
Oil-soaked or heat-damaged connector on the cylinder head
Damaged CAN wiring between module and engine controller
Rocker arm control module internally faulty

U011C.d: U011C is the partner of U011B for rocker arm control module B, for example the controller of the second cylinder bank or of a second group of switchable rocker arms where the task is split across two units. The engine controller expects cyclic status from it, such as the confirmed lock state per cylinder, and records U011C once those frames fail to arrive.
s: MIL on
Affected cylinders remain in full-lift mode
Uneven running or higher consumption
c: Module B without power or ground
Contaminated or loose connector at the second cylinder head
Open or shorted CAN lines to module B
Rocker arm control module B internally faulty

U011D.d: U011D signals a lost all-wheel-drive control module. In contrast to a single coupling controller (U0114) or a transfer case module (U0102), this unit manages an entire on-demand AWD system, deciding when and how much torque goes to the secondary axle, which in some cars is driven by its own electric motor.
s: AWD warning lamp or message
Drive on one axle only
Stability control may also show a warning
c: AWD module without power or ground
Water or corrosion at the module connector near the rear axle
Chafed or open CAN wiring to the module

U011E.d: U011E reports that the controller for throttle actuator B has gone silent. Most engines use a single electronic throttle whose motor the engine controller drives itself; a separately housed throttle controller is covered by U0107.
s: MIL on
Limp-home mode with reduced power
Poor throttle response or idle only
c: Throttle B controller without power or ground
Damaged CAN wiring or connector to the controller
Throttle actuator B control module internally faulty

U011F.d: U011F concerns the V2X module, the radio unit through which a car exchanges messages with other vehicles, roadside infrastructure, pedestrians' devices or the network (vehicle-to-everything), either via short-range DSRC/ITS-G5 or via cellular C-V2X. It passes alerts such as an approaching hazard or signal-phase information on to the driver and to assistance systems.
s: Connected traffic and hazard warnings unavailable
Possible service message in the cluster
c: V2X module without power or ground
Damaged bus wiring or connector, e.g. after roof or antenna work
Software or configuration fault in the V2X or gateway module

U0120.d: U0120 means the starter/generator control module, which drives an electric machine that can both crank the engine and produce electrical power, has dropped off the bus. Mitsubishi documents it for the Outlander PHEV (2018 and 2022): the hybrid controller (PHEV-ECU) sets U0120 when, after its supply has been within 10–16 V for more than 5 s, no frames from the generator control unit (GCU) housed within the power drive
s: MIL and hybrid or charging warning
Start-stop or engine start by the electric machine unavailable
Battery not charged while driving
c: Fault on the CAN lines between hybrid controller and generator control unit
Starter/generator control unit faulty (replacement if it stores U0120 itself)
Low 12 V supply or poor ground at the power electronics

U0121.d: U0121 is stored by any listener that stops receiving the ABS/ESC module, so it often shows up in engine, transmission, cluster and gateway at once. GM treats it as Type C without MIL (Chrysler bulletins list it with MIL): the 2019 LTG engine table watches frames $0C1/$0C5 (0.5 s) and the 2025 TCM table waits over 10 s; while it is active, the ECM skips wheel-speed plausibility checks.
s: ABS, ESC and brake warning lamps on
Speedometer or gear display erratic, several U codes
Reduced brake assistance or vehicle stays in Park
Start-stop and driver assistance unavailable
c: Water ingress or corroded terminals at the ABS/EBCM connector
Poor ground point or supply fuse of the ABS module
ABS/ESC software that fails to wake up or restarts (update released)

U0122.d: U0122 tells you that a networked controller, often the engine or hybrid ECU, has stopped receiving the cyclic frames of the stability control unit (ESC/VSC/ASC, usually combined with the ABS hydraulic unit). Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV documents it in the PHEV-ECU: with 10–16 V present for at least 5 s and the motor switch on, a broken link to the ABS/ASC unit lasting 2 s or more stores U0122-00, and Mitsubishi
s: ESC, traction control and ABS warning lamps on
Stability and traction control unavailable
MIL on in some vehicles (engine or hybrid ECU stores the code)
c: Missing fuse, supply or ground at the stability/ABS unit
Damaged CAN wiring or faulty gateway between the bus segments
Receiving controller software reports the loss too eagerly (update exists, e.g. Subaru)

U0123.d: U0123 is stored when the stability controller or another listener misses the messages of a networked yaw rate sensor, the unit that measures how fast the car rotates around its vertical axis. Without that signal ESC cannot compare the actual turn with the steering input.
s: ESC and traction control warning lamps on
Stability control switched off for the rest of the trip
Often stored together with U0124 when both signals come from one housing
c: Loose or corroded connector at the yaw rate sensor (often under the centre console or seat)
Fuse, supply or ground of the sensor module missing
Damaged chassis CAN wiring to the sensor
Yaw rate sensor module internally failed

U0124.d: With U0124 a controller reports that the frames from the lateral acceleration sensor module have stopped. This sensor tells the stability system how strongly the vehicle is being pushed sideways in a bend; together with yaw rate and steering angle it lets ESC detect skidding.
s: ESC/traction warning lamp lit
Stability control deactivated
Frequently logged together with U0123
c: Corroded or loose plug at the acceleration sensor module
Power or ground of the sensor module interrupted
Chafed bus wires on the way to the sensor

U0125.d: U0125 concerns the inertial measurement unit that bundles yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration on one bus node. GM uses the code widely: the 2019 XT4 brake controller (EBCM) flags a missing IMU frame after 0.1 s, the 2025 object-detection module after 0.05 s and then disables adaptive cruise; both are Type C without MIL.
s: Service ESC / StabiliTrak message, traction and ABS lamps
Adaptive cruise control or all-wheel drive unavailable
Electric parking brake warning on some models
c: Wire broken inside the insulation or rubbed through near a chassis connector (GM X411)
Loose or corroded plug at the inertial sensor
Brake controller software that drops the sensor (reflash released)

U0126.d: U0126 means the steering wheel angle sensor, usually mounted on the steering column, is no longer heard on the bus. ESC needs this value to know the path the driver intends.
s: ESC and traction lamps on, stability control inactive
Check engine lamp on some models
Lane or park assist functions unavailable
c: Loose or damaged connector or clock-spring harness at the steering column
Power or ground of the steering angle sensor missing
Module software reporting the fault wrongly or after remote start (update)
Steering angle sensor faulty; recalibration needed after replacement

U0127.d: U0127 is logged when the tyre pressure monitoring module, the receiver that collects the radio signals of the wheel sensors, stops answering on the vehicle network. In the VW group the gateway (address 0019) stores it: Audi bulletin 2065474 for A6/A7/RS 6/RS 7 2019–2022 finds the module J502 unreachable and blames moisture entering through its pressure equalisation element; the fix is a new module and bracket.
s: TPMS warning lamp or message in the cluster
Tyre pressures not displayed
Scan tool cannot reach the TPMS module
c: Moisture inside the TPMS module through its vent element
Pins, power or ground at the TPMS module connector faulty
Damaged bus wiring to the module

U0128.d: U0128 signals that the electric parking brake controller has dropped off the bus. GM rates it very differently by node: the 2017 engine table waits 10 s for the park brake message and treats a miss as Type A (MIL at once), while the 2019 chassis controller (ICCM) needs only 1 s but files it as Type C without MIL; from model year 2018 GM folds this ICCM check into U0121.
s: Service Parking Brake message or brake warning lamp
Electric parking brake does not apply or release
MIL on in vehicles where the engine controller stores it
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the park brake module missing
Chafed or corroded bus wiring, often affecting several modules at once
Weak battery causing the module to drop out (stored code)
Controller software issue fixed by reprogramming
Park brake control module internally faulty

U0129.d: U0129 points to the brake system control module A, in GM vehicles the OBD node with diagnostic ID 7E5. GM's 2019 LTG engine table checks frames $0C1, $0C5, $0D1, $1C6 and others every 500 ms (one of them 10 s) and needs two trips to set the MIL; the 2018 hybrid controller and the 2025 ECM treat it as Type A, the 2017 table as Special Type C.
s: MIL or service engine lamp plus brake/ESC warnings
Gear selection or stop-start blocked on some vehicles
Several other U codes stored at the same time
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the brake control module faulty
Low battery or jump start leaving stored network codes (ECM update released)
Damaged or corroded CAN wiring to the brake module
Brake system control module internally faulty

U012A.d: U012A reports that chassis control module A is silent. The unit behind the letter A varies between brands; GM uses the code in several engine and transmission tables.
s: MIL on in vehicles where the engine controller logs it
Chassis functions controlled by module A unavailable
Hard start or stalling if the module drives the fuel pump
c: Power, ground or fuse of chassis module A missing
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Voltage dip leaving a stored code

U012B.d: U012B is the counterpart to U012A for a second chassis controller, labelled B. No manufacturer documents U012B in an openly available source, so its exact job (air suspension, damping, steering or another chassis task) depends on the vehicle.
s: Chassis warning message in the cluster
Functions handled by module B (e.g. suspension) unavailable
Scan tool cannot reach module B
c: Fuse, power or ground of chassis module B interrupted
Damaged bus line or connector to module B
Chassis module B internally faulty or not programmed

U012C.d: U012C covers the controller that drives active engine mounts or inertial shakers to cancel engine vibration, for example in cars that switch off cylinders. Such a unit needs engine speed and load from the network to generate a counter-phase force; a Honda patent (US 10360893) describes a separate AVC control unit with actuators and acceleration sensors that adapts its cancelling output to engine rotation.
s: Noticeable engine vibration at idle or in cylinder deactivation mode
Humming or booming noise in the cabin
Fuel saving mode may stay disabled
c: Power or ground of the vibration control unit missing
Bus wire or connector damaged near engine or subframe
Active vibration control module internally faulty

U012D.d: U012D is stored when the powertrain controller loses contact with the regulator of generator A. In many Ford models this is the smart alternator, which the PCM commands over a LIN line that it often shares with the active grille shutters; for that reason U012D usually shows up together with U0284/U0285 and U042E.
s: Check Charging System message or battery lamp
MIL on in some models
Battery discharges, voltage unstable
Active grille shutter codes stored as well
c: Water or corrosion in a connector of the shared LIN line (grille shutter, C202)
LIN wire chafed and shorted to ground near an engine mount bracket
Generator regulator internally faulty or without supply

U012E.d: U012E applies to engines whose camshaft phaser is driven by its own electronic unit rather than an oil control solenoid, as with electric intake valve timing. Mitsubishi bulletin TSB-23-11-003 for the 2022 Outlander lists U012E next to U0101, U0122, U0146, U0155 and U042F as communication codes of the engine controller and links it in the warranty chart to the electric intake valve timing control module circuit.
s: MIL on
Reduced power and poorer response, especially at low engine speed
Rough idle or higher fuel consumption
c: Power or ground of the electric valve timing module interrupted
CAN wiring or connector at the engine damaged by heat or oil
Camshaft position control module internally faulty

U012F.d: U012F is reserved for vehicles with a second generator, labelled B, whose regulator or control electronics talk to the powertrain or hybrid controller over a bus. That can be a second alternator on heavy-duty trucks or a further motor-generator in a hybrid drive.
s: Charging system warning
Battery voltage falls during driving
Hybrid system warning or reduced electric drive on hybrids
c: Wet or corroded connector in the bus line to generator B
Fuse, power or ground of the generator B electronics missing
Bus wire chafed against engine or bracket
Generator B regulator or control module faulty

U0130.d: U0130 is logged when a controller on the network stops hearing the steering effort control module, which varies how much assistance the driver gets at the wheel, usually depending on road speed. Saab's 2011 9-5 code list maps U0130 to its electric power steering control module and adds failure-type bytes 71 (data not valid), 72 (message counter wrong) and 74 (checksum error), while a separate power steering module ke
s: Steering system warning lamp or message
Steering feels heavier or no longer adapts to speed
Further communication codes stored in several modules
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the steering effort module missing
Damaged CAN wiring or loose connector at the steering module
Module configuration or software not matched after a repair (e.g. Ford after HV battery replacement)

U0131.d: U0131 means a listener on the bus has missed the cyclic frames of power steering control module A, normally the electric steering unit on rack or column. GM documents several receivers: the ECM of 2019 models flags it after 10 s without message $1E5 as a Type C, emissions-neutral fault and then stops basing auto-stop decisions on steering angle; the EBCM reacts after 0.025 s, and the 2025 EOCM3 after 0.05–0.25 s, swi
s: Reduced or no steering assist, heavy steering
EPS or steering fault message in the cluster
Adaptive cruise control switched off (GM)
Check-engine lamp on some vehicles (e.g. Jeep)
c: High-current fuse, supply or ground of the steering module open (e.g. Ford mega fuse F2)
Chafed or damaged harness on the bus or wake-up line (e.g. Jeep Cherokee, GM circuit 5986)
Steering module software, fixed by an update (Ford Super Duty 2020)
Power steering control module internally failed

U0132.d: U0132 is set when a module stops receiving suspension control module A, the controller for air springs, ride height or damping. GM names the K5 automatic level control module of 2021 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon with air suspension: it goes silent, a leveling or headlamp service message comes up, and removing two fuses for a few minutes revives it (PIT5795).
s: Air suspension or leveling warning in the cluster
Ride height control or headlamp leveling inoperative
MIL on some vehicles (e.g. Ram heavy duty)
c: Suspension module locked up, recovers after a power cycle (GM PIT5795, Bentley)
Suspension module software, fixed by an update (FCA Ram, Audi J775)
Fuse, supply or CAN wiring of the suspension module faulty

U0133.d: U0133 indicates that the active roll control module, which drives hydraulic or electromechanical anti-roll bars to reduce body lean in corners, no longer answers on the bus. No manufacturer publicly ties U0133 to that module: Saab's 2011 9-5 list uses the number for its air suspension control module instead, so older vehicles may interpret it differently.
s: Chassis or suspension warning lamp
More body roll when cornering
Sport or dynamic driving modes unavailable
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the roll control module faulty
Software of master and stabiliser units not compatible after a replacement (Bentley TPI 2055643)

U0134.d: U0134 is stored when a controller loses contact with the rear power steering control module, the actuator unit of a rear-wheel or four-wheel steering system. Such systems turn the rear wheels by a few degrees, opposite to the front ones at low speed for a smaller turning circle and in the same direction at higher speed for calmer lane changes.
s: Steering system warning lamp or message
Larger turning circle, rear wheels no longer steer
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the rear steering module faulty
Corroded or wet connector at the rear axle actuator
Rear steering control module internally faulty

U0135.d: U0135 reports that the front differential control module has dropped off the network. Such a module operates an electronically controlled clutch pack or locker in the front axle, either to move torque from one front wheel to the other or to lock both for traction off road.
s: 4WD, locker or traction warning lamp
Front locker or torque vectoring not available
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the front differential module faulty
Water or corrosion in the connector near the front axle
Front differential control module internally faulty

U0136.d: U0136 is set when a listener misses the rear differential control module, which operates an electronic limited-slip or twin-clutch rear drive unit. GM's 2019 tables document it in the ECM of the Cadillac XT4 (LSY engine): if message $1CF from the rear drive module stays absent for 10 s while bus A is active and supply exceeds 11 V, the ECM stores U0136 as a Type B fault, so the MIL comes on after two trips.
s: AWD or rear differential warning
Car drives with front-wheel drive only, less traction
MIL after two trips on GM vehicles
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the rear drive module faulty
Corroded or damaged connector at the rear axle, exposed to spray water
Rear differential control module internally faulty

U0137.d: U0137 means the trailer brake control module, which energises a towed trailer’s electric brakes in step with the tow vehicle's braking, is missing on the bus. Ford uses the code widely: on 2022 F-150 trucks without that module the ABS unit may store U0137 by mistake, and it can then be ignored (SSM 50418); on F-150, Expedition, Navigator and Ranger of 2021–2024 the IPC, BCM or PSCM log it together with a warning that
s: Trailer brake fault message in the cluster
Trailer brakes not applied or gain control inoperative
Park assist disabled on some Ram trucks
c: Trailer or ABS module software, fixed by reprogramming (Ford SSM 53236, 50418)
Improperly seated connector, damaged harness or water intrusion at the module (FCA 9004253)
Module retrofitted or configured incorrectly (dealer-installed tow package)
Trailer brake control module internally faulty

U0138.d: U0138 is logged when another module no longer receives the all-terrain control module, the unit behind the selector that lets the driver pick a terrain or drive mode such as snow, sand or mud and then adapts traction control, throttle response and shift points. Ford lists U0138 in the OBD code tables of its 2014 vehicles and marks it as available in all three self-test modes, without an entry in the lamp column.
s: Terrain or drive mode cannot be selected
4WD or traction control warning lamp
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the terrain module faulty
Loose or corroded connector at the module or the mode selector

U0139.d: U0139 reports lost contact with suspension control module B, at GM the semi-active damping system (SADS). GM's 2025 tables let the ECM watch two SADS messages, $035 with a 10 s limit and $364 with 325 ms, and set U0139 as Type B with the MIL after two trips; the EBCM treats missing damper frames for 250 ms as Type C.
s: Check-engine lamp, often without any other symptom (GM)
Service Suspension message, adaptive damping inactive
Harsher or softer ride than usual
c: Suspension module software locks up, recovers after a fuse reset (GM PIT6007)
High resistance or open in the module wake-up line (GM circuit 5986)
Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the damping module faulty
Suspension control module B internally faulty

U013C.d: U013C applies to an accelerator pedal module that reports over a data bus instead of analog sensor lines. In a drive-by-wire system the pedal module carries the driver's torque request to the engine or drive controller, so that controller has to fall back to a safe state as soon as the pedal messages disappear.
s: No response to the accelerator, engine stays at idle
Reduced power warning
MIL on depending on the manufacturer
c: Loose or corroded connector at the pedal module (footwell moisture)
Supply, ground or bus wiring of the pedal module faulty

U013D.d: U013D stands for lost communication with vacuum sensor A, a networked sensor that reports the vacuum in the brake booster or a vacuum reservoir. Engines with little manifold vacuum, such as turbocharged direct-injection units, and hybrids use this value to switch on an electric vacuum pump or to throttle the engine so the brake assist stays sufficient.
s: Brake booster or brake assist warning
Electric vacuum pump runs constantly or start-stop disabled
MIL on depending on the manufacturer
c: Loose or corroded connector at the vacuum sensor on the booster
Supply, ground or bus wiring of the sensor faulty

U013E.d: U013E concerns vacuum sensor B, the second networked vacuum sensor in vehicles that measure at more than one point, for example in the booster chamber and in a separate reservoir, or that read a redundant value. The receiving module, typically the engine or brake controller, sets the code when the frames of this sensor stop arriving.
s: Brake system or brake assist warning
Often stored together with U013D when both sensors share wiring
c: Loose or corroded connector at vacuum sensor B
Supply, ground or bus wiring shared with sensor A faulty

U013F.d: U013F reports that the pedestrian alert control module has gone silent. Electric and hybrid cars need it to produce a warning sound at low speed, because they are otherwise almost inaudible; FMVSS 141 in the US and UN R138 in Europe make such a sound mandatory.
s: No warning sound when driving slowly
Pedestrian alert fault message in the cluster
c: Water or corrosion at the module, a speaker or their connectors
Supply, ground or LIN/CAN wiring of the module faulty
Pedestrian alert control module internally faulty

U0140.d: U0140 is among the most frequent network codes: a listening controller misses the frames of the body control module, which handles lights, locks, wipers and often the power mode that wakes other units. The code sits in the listener, not in the BCM.
s: Lights, central locking, wipers or interior lamps misbehave or fail
Radio, climate controls or gauges blank or erratic
Same code stored in several modules at once
MIL on in some vehicles (GM 2025 Type B, FCA PCM)
c: BCM fuse, power feed or ground missing or corroded
Chafed bus line or loose, wet connector between BCM and the listening modules
Weak battery, jump start or voltage dip leaves a stored history code
BCM or listener software or configuration out of date (Ford SSM 47040, FCA 18-013-22)

U0141.d: U0141 names the first of several body controllers. Unlike U0140, which stands for the single main BCM, the letter suits cars that spread body tasks over more units, and each maker decides which one is A.
s: Keyless entry, liftgate or other body functions inoperative
Ignition cannot be switched on (Audi e-tron case)
MIL or several warning lamps on
Code stored in many modules at once
c: Power, fuse or ground of body module A missing
Software of module A or of the listener needs updating (Audi J393, FCA PCM)
Bus wire or connector to module A damaged or loose

U0142.d: U0142 reports that a second body controller, labelled B, has stopped talking. No maker explains publicly which unit carries this letter; depending on the design it may be a rear body module, a power distribution box or a comfort unit next to the main BCM (U0140) and module A (U0141).
s: Body functions handled by module B do not work
Scan tool cannot reach module B
Often only a stored code without noticeable fault
c: Module B without power: fuse, transport short pin or relay missing
Flat battery or battery disconnect leaves a history code
Damaged bus wire or loose connector to module B

U0143.d: With U0143 a listener reports that body controller C has gone quiet. The letter only means a third body unit; its role is set by the maker.
s: Often none; code found only during a scan
Functions of module C (for example trailer-related outputs) unavailable
Scan tool cannot reach module C
c: Software parameters in the listening module (Ford F-150 trailer module)
Power, fuse or ground of module C missing
Bus line or connector to module C damaged

U0144.d: U0144 is logged by one or more control units that no longer receive the cyclic messages of the body controller J2012 calls Body Control Module D. In GM's network logic every node broadcasts a state-of-health message with ignition on; if it stays away while the supply is between 9 and 16 V, the listeners store a code naming the silent unit, not themselves.
s: Body functions handled by module D (locks, lighting, seats) do not respond
Scan tool cannot reach module D
Same code stored in several other modules
c: Fuse, power or ground of the body module D missing
Chafed bus wire or loose, wet connector on the way to module D
Weak battery or voltage dip, so the module drops off the bus (history code)
Body module D internally faulty or not programmed

U0145.d: U0145 means the network has lost contact with the body controller J2012 labels E. Receiving modules expect its periodic messages; GM's generic logic sets such a code when a supervised message carrying the sender's availability fails to arrive at 9-16 V.
s: Individual body functions such as lights or locks inoperative
Code appears together with U0140 in several modules
Fault comes and goes when the harness is moved
c: Loose, spread or pushed-out terminal in the bus harness (Stellantis case)
Open or short on the LIN/CAN line to module E
Power or ground of module E missing
Body module E or BCM internally faulty

U0146.d: U0146 means the first gateway, the node that routes messages between bus segments, is silent; GM calls it serial data gateway module, Ford, Audi and GM's tables just Gateway A. GM's 2019 ECM expects message $3CF at least every 10 s with the battery above 11 V and treats a gap as Type B, so the MIL lights if it recurs on a second trip.
s: Instrument cluster gauges dead or fluctuating
No crank, no start or stalling
Many U-codes in several modules and multiple warning messages
MIL on (GM Type B)
c: Gateway software hangs and stops routing although powered (GM PIT5586G, Audi ICAS)
Bent, backed-out or loose terminals at the gateway connectors
Gateway fuse, power or ground missing

U0147.d: U0147 points to a second gateway, B. Large vehicle networks often use more than one routing node, for example a central gateway plus a separate unit that connects the car to the outside world.
s: Connected services, emergency call or remote app functions unavailable
Modules behind gateway B not reachable with a scan tool
Further codes such as radio communication or antenna faults
c: Power, fuse or ground of gateway B missing
Bus wiring or connector to gateway B faulty
Telematics unit acting as gateway B faulty or in a fault state (FCA)
Gateway B software hangs after an update or voltage dip

U0148.d: U0148 reports that the third gateway, Gateway C, has gone silent. A gateway links separate bus segments (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and forwards messages between them, so when it drops out, every module behind it disappears too.
s: Several modules behind the gateway unreachable at once
Many U-codes stored across the vehicle
Multiple warning lamps or messages in the cluster
c: Fuse, power or ground of gateway C missing
Damaged bus wiring or corroded connector at gateway C
Gateway C software fault or incomplete programming

U0149.d: U0149 names Gateway D as the module whose messages no longer arrive. Vehicles with several gateways split the network into domains, and each gateway routes traffic between its own bus segments; losing D therefore cuts off the domain it serves.
s: Group of modules in one domain does not answer
Many U-codes stored at the same time
Functions of the cut-off domain inoperative
c: Gateway D without power or ground
Open or shorted bus wiring, wet or corroded connector at gateway D
Low battery voltage or battery disconnect (history code only)

U014A.d: U014A concerns a third battery energy control module, C. Hybrid and electric vehicles use such units to watch cell voltages, temperatures and state of charge and to protect the pack; distributed or modular designs give several sub-packs their own controller, which is where letters beyond A and B come in.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning, reduced power
Charging refused or stopped
Vehicle may not enter ready mode
c: Low-voltage supply, fuse or ground of battery module C missing
Bus wiring or connector inside or at the battery pack damaged or corroded
Moisture or coolant in the pack affecting module C
Battery module C internally faulty or not programmed

U014B.d: U014B covers the vehicle-side controller of a wireless charging system. Inductive charging transfers energy without a plug, through a coil in a ground pad and a receiving coil under the car; the SAE J2954 standard, finalised in 2020, defines power classes of 3.7, 7.7 and 11 kW and relies on resonant coupling with about 85 percent efficiency.
s: Wireless charging does not start or stops
Charging warning message, cable charging still works
Module not reachable with a scan tool
c: Supply, fuse or ground of the inductive charging module missing
Wiring or connector to the underbody receiver damaged by water, salt or impact
Software of module and charge controller not matching

U014C.d: U014C is the fourth slot in the battery controller family and points at module D. Such a letter is only needed where a pack is split into many sub-packs with their own monitoring boards, or where a vehicle carries an extra battery, for example a second traction pack or a separate 48 V unit, each reporting to a master controller.
s: Battery or hybrid system warning
Reduced drive power or no ready mode
Charging not possible
c: Supply or ground of battery module D missing
Internal pack communication line or connector to D faulty
Master controller configured for a module D that does not match

U014D.d: U014D concerns the second networked mirror unit. Modern mirrors carry motors for adjustment and folding, a heating element, auto-dimming glass, turn-signal repeaters or blind-spot lamps, and the electronics for them often sit on the bus as their own node.
s: Mirror adjustment, folding or heating inoperative on one side
Blind-spot or turn-signal lamp in the mirror dark
Often no other effect; code found during a scan
c: Broken wire in the flexing harness between body and door
Fuse, power or ground of mirror module B missing
Vehicle configuration expects a mirror module that is not fitted (FCA case for module A)
Water ingress or impact damage in the mirror housing

U014E.d: U014E concerns a second inertial sensor module, B. Such a unit combines accelerometers and gyroscopes, measures turning rate and acceleration across and along the car, and sends the values over the bus.
s: Stability control or traction warning on
Driver assistance such as adaptive cruise unavailable
Normal braking unaffected
c: Connector or wiring of sensor module B corroded or broken
Power or ground of module B missing
Receiving controller software not matching module B

U0150.d: U0150 is the last code of the gateway block and points at Gateway E. Gateways are central nodes that connect bus systems of different speed and type and forward only the messages each side needs.
s: Modules routed through gateway E not reachable by the scan tool
Several functions fail together
Warning messages in the instrument cluster
c: Gateway E fuse blown or ground loose
Bus line to gateway E chafed or connector corroded
Gateway E software fault, update or reprogramming needed

U0151.d: U0151 means the airbag control module, which reads crash sensors and fires airbags and belt pretensioners, no longer reaches a listener. Names vary: GM and Saab say sensing and diagnostic module, FCA occupant restraint controller, Honda SRS unit.
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Airbags may not deploy in a crash if the module has failed
Several warning lamps or MIL on (Dodge Charger 2024)
Scan tool cannot communicate with the airbag module
c: Airbag module fuse, ground or connector faulty (often under the seat or centre console)
Airbag control module internally failed (Honda Accord 2008-10)
Airbag module software needs updating (Dodge Charger 2024)
Another node blocks the bus, for example a faulty head-up display (Mazda CX-3)

U0152.d: U0152 is the left-hand partner of U0153: a separate controller for the side restraints on the left no longer sends. In most cars side impacts are detected by satellite sensors in sills, B- or C-pillars that feed the central airbag unit; Bosch, for example, mounts its peripheral acceleration sensors on the left and right of the body and links them over the PSI5 sensor interface.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side or curtain airbag possibly not ready
Code stored in the main airbag module
c: Connector under the left seat or in the pillar loose or corroded
Power or ground of the left side module missing
Water ingress at the sill or door damaging wiring or module
Left side restraints module internally faulty

U0153.d: U0153 means the airbag system no longer hears from the separate control module for the right-side restraints. Some vehicles split the job: a central airbag unit plus side units that evaluate side impact sensors and fire side or curtain bags.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side or curtain airbag may not deploy
Scan tool cannot reach the right side module
c: Loose or corroded connector at the right side module (B-pillar or under the seat)
Power or ground of the right side module missing
Bus wiring damaged after seat or trim work

U0154.d: U0154 is stored when the occupant classification module goes silent. This unit evaluates sensors in the front passenger seat, such as a weight mat or pressure bladder, and tells the airbag controller whether the seat is empty, holds a child seat or an adult, so that the passenger airbag can be suppressed or allowed.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag on/off indicator wrong or flashing
Passenger airbag deactivated or in a default state
c: Connector under the passenger seat loose, damaged or pulled during seat work
Power or ground of the classification module missing
Classification module or seat sensor internally faulty
Network wake-up timing or software issue (Mercedes-AMG 2023)

U0155.d: U0155 says a listener no longer receives the instrument cluster, which shows speed and warnings and on many cars also produces chimes and turn-signal ticks. The cause is not always the cluster: on 2017 GM full-size trucks and SUVs several modules logged U0155 when the serial data gateway hung, so dead gauges came from the gateway (PIT5586G).
s: Gauges dead, frozen or sweeping
No chimes or turn-signal ticking
MIL on in some vehicles (Honda 2021-22, Ford Explorer 2020)
Several warning lamps and codes in many modules
c: Cluster fuse, ground or connector behind the dash faulty
Gateway hangs and stops forwarding cluster messages (GM PIT5586G)
Software of another module causes false loss of communication (Honda 21-021, Ford SSM 49218)

U0156.d: U0156 concerns information center A, the display and infotainment unit that shows messages, audio, navigation or vehicle settings. Two makers document the code.
s: Center display black, no audio or navigation
Network malfunction or several warning messages in the cluster
Climate or vehicle settings that run through the screen unavailable
c: Supply fuse of the unit missing or not fully seated (Mazda SA-040/24)
Infotainment unit internally faulty, for example memory chip (Volvo TJ 25872)
Infotainment software hangs or needs an update
Bus wiring or connector behind the dash faulty

U0157.d: U0157 is set when the second information display, Information Center B, stops transmitting on the vehicle bus. J2012 provides two such driver information displays, A (U0156) and B, separate from the instrument cluster (U0155) and the head-up display (U0158); which screen counts as B is up to the manufacturer.
s: Secondary display dark, frozen or showing no data
Messages normally shown on display B missing
Code stored in several modules
c: Display unit B without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus line or connector behind the dashboard damaged
Display software hang or failed update

U0158.d: U0158 means the head-up display, which projects speed, navigation arrows or warnings into the windscreen, has stopped answering the module that supervises it, usually the instrument cluster. GM lists it in the Saab 9-5 (2011) U-code table and covers it in bulletin 22-NA-113: on 2020-2022 Cadillac CT4/CT5 with RPO UV6 the cluster stores U0158 when LIN messages arrive at an awkward moment while the HUD enters standby,
s: Head-up display blank or frozen
Brightness, height or page settings have no effect
Display returns after an ignition cycle
c: HUD stuck in standby due to message timing, cured by cluster software (GM CT4/CT5)
Stored entry from transport/logistics mode on new vehicles (Stellantis)
HUD fuse, supply or ground interrupted
LIN/CAN line or connector under the dashboard faulty

U0159.d: U0159 reports that parking assist control module A, which evaluates the ultrasonic sensors and drives the distance warnings, has fallen silent. GM spells out the check for the brake module: the 2019 Cadillac XT4 EBCM (19OBDG03D) and the 2020 brake module tables (20OBDG03C) set it when the automatic-parking braking request is missing for more than 0.25 s, Type C, no MIL.
s: Park assist unavailable or Service Parking Assist message
Park assist switch cannot turn the system on or off
Code stored in brake module, cluster or BCM
c: Park assist module software fault, fixed by reprogramming (GM PIT5507E, 20-NA-099)
Modules on different software levels (Stellantis S2108000149)
Park assist module without power or ground
Harmless entry after remote start or wake-up (Ford, VW)
Bus line or connector in the bumper/rear area damaged

U015A.d: U015A concerns a second anti-lock brake controller, module B. Vehicles prepared for automated driving need braking that still works after a single fault, so suppliers pair two independent units, for example Bosch's iBooster with the ESP control unit.
s: Brake system or driver assistance warning in the cluster
Automated driving or adaptive cruise functions unavailable
Code stored in the primary brake controller
c: Brake module B without power or ground (own fuse in redundant layouts)
Bus line or connector to module B in the engine bay corroded or open
Brake modules on incompatible software after repair
ABS control module B internally faulty

U015B.d: U015B is set when the second power steering controller, module B, stops sending. Redundant steering for automated driving splits the electronics into two paths so one can keep assisting if the other fails; Bosch describes such a fail-operational design with an electrical fallback giving roughly half the normal assist.
s: Steering system warning in the cluster
Lane centring or automated steering unavailable
Steering assist possibly reduced
c: Steering module B without power or ground (separate supply path)
Connector at the steering rack or column wet, loose or corroded
Steering modules not matched after replacement or update
Power steering control module B internally faulty

U015C.d: U015C points to automated driving system control module A, the computer that fuses camera and radar data for adaptive cruise, lane centring and emergency braking. Stellantis documents it in detail.
s: Automatic Emergency Braking Unavailable message
Adaptive cruise and lane settings not stored between drives
MIL on (Stellantis)
c: Software in front radar or ADAS decision module outdated (Stellantis TSBs)
Ethernet cable routed too tight, connector pins loosened
ADS control module A without power or ground
ADS control module A internally faulty

U015D.d: U015D names automated driving system control module B. Where the driving assistance computer is split into two halves, each half and the navigation and motion module watch the other over Ethernet.
s: Blindspot Alert Unavailable message
Blind-spot lamps in the mirrors stay lit
Driver assistance features disabled intermittently
c: Ethernet harness too taut, pins pushed out or fretted (Stellantis S2508000095)
Harness clip in wrong position, connectors under strain
ADS control module B without power or ground
ADS control module B internally faulty

U015E.d: U015E concerns interface module A, the link that passes commands from an automated driving computer to the base vehicle's brakes, steering and powertrain and reports their state back. Such interfaces belong to the act layer of the sense-think-act chain that Bosch uses to describe automated driving.
s: Automated driving mode cannot be activated
Takeover request or controlled stop during automated driving
Driver assistance warning in the cluster
c: Interface module A without power or ground
Bus or Ethernet connection to the interface damaged or strained
Interface and automation computer on mismatched software

U015F.d: U015F is the companion code for automated driving system interface module B. A second interface lets a fail-operational design keep a path to the vehicle actuators when the first one drops out, which matters most above SAE level 2, where the system rather than the driver watches the road.
s: Automated driving unavailable, redundancy fault message
Request to take over steering and braking
Code stored in the automation computer
c: Interface module B fuse, supply or ground faulty
Connector or line of the redundant bus path damaged
Module B not updated together with the other ADS modules

U0160.d: U0160 is stored when the audible alert module, the unit that produces chimes for an open door, unfastened belt, key left in or lights on, drops off the bus. GM uses it: the Saab 9-5 (2011) U-code list calls the unit Chime Alarm Control Module, and by GM's generic procedure the code appears once the chime unit's cyclic status frame stays away while the supply is within 9 to 16 V.
s: No chime for open door, belt or lights
Chime sounds continuously or at wrong times
Code stored in the BCM or cluster
c: Chime module fuse blown or ground loose
Connector or bus line behind the dashboard damaged
Vehicle configured for a separate chime module that is not fitted

U0161.d: U0161 says the compass module no longer reports. In many vehicles the electronic compass sits in the interior mirror or the overhead console: a pair of perpendicular magnetic sensors measures the earth's field, and the module sends the heading to a display.
s: Compass heading missing or shown as dashes
Compass calibration not possible
Code stored in the cluster or overhead module
c: Compass module or mirror without power or ground
Connector at the mirror or headliner loose, e.g. after windscreen replacement
Data line in the A-pillar or headliner damaged
Compass module or mirror electronics faulty

U0162.d: U0162 indicates that the navigation display, typically the screen unit of the head unit, no longer answers. Subaru documents it in two settings.
s: Navigation screen dark or not responding
Rear vehicle detection warning lamp on (Subaru)
Several communication codes stored at once
c: Supply interrupted, e.g. loose terminal at the fuse box (Subaru TechTIPS)
Software of the receiving module, e.g. rear radar control unit (Subaru 07-205-22)
Connector behind the head unit loose after radio work
Navigation display or head unit faulty

U0163.d: U0163 is logged when the navigation control module, the computer that works out position and route, stops communicating. In many cars this function is built into the head unit, in others it is a separate box behind the trim.
s: Navigation and route guidance unavailable
Turn arrows missing in the cluster or head-up display
Code stored in the cluster or other display modules
c: Navigation unit fuse, supply or ground faulty
Connector at the head unit or navigation box loose or corroded
Navigation software hang or failed map/software update

U0164.d: U0164 is stored by any module that stops hearing the HVAC control module, the unit that runs blower, flaps and temperature selection. GM documents two monitors in its 2025 tables (25OBDG03B): the body control module watches several HVAC frames and flags a gap longer than 12.5 s at 11-18 V, and the central gateway reacts after 6.5 s once a frame is overdue by 2.5 times its period; both are Type B, so the MIL can come
s: Climate control panel dark or not responding
Blower, temperature or defrost stuck at last setting
Check engine light on some GM models after two trips
Code stored in several modules at once
c: Loose or spread terminals at gateway or inline bus connectors
HVAC module without power or ground
Incomplete module configuration or hung module, cleared by battery reset (Ford)

U0165.d: U0165 names a second climate unit, the rear HVAC control module, fitted in vans, minivans and large SUVs that heat and cool the back rows with their own blower and flaps. The code says this rear module has gone quiet on the network; the front unit is covered by U0164.
s: Rear climate controls without function
Rear blower stuck off or at one speed
Front climate keeps working normally
c: Rear HVAC module without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring to the rear unit chafed under trim or at sliding-door area
Vehicle coded for rear climate that is not fitted

U0166.d: U0166 reports that the auxiliary heater control module has stopped communicating. Such heaters, burning fuel or working electrically, warm the coolant or the cabin air before or during a drive and are common on diesels and cold-climate packages.
s: Auxiliary or parking heater does not start
Slow engine and cabin warm-up in cold weather
Code stored in the engine or climate controller
c: Heater module fuse blown or ground corroded (often underbody mounting)
Corroded heater connector from road splash
Bus line to the heater damaged

U0167.d: U0167 means the vehicle immobilizer control module, which checks the transponder in the key and then releases the engine controller, can no longer be heard on the bus. Since the key handshake cannot complete, the engine typically cranks without firing or does not crank at all.
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or no crank
Immobilizer or key symbol flashes
Key not recognised
c: Immobilizer module or antenna ring without power or ground
Interrupted or faulty immobilizer software update (Triumph 2024)
Bus or connector at the steering column damaged

U0168.d: U0168 points to the vehicle security control module, which handles anti-theft and key authorisation and in many layouts also hosts the immobilizer handshake. Chrysler shows the link: its 2011 field report names U0168 for the SKREEM/WCM, and bulletin 18-023-13 (Grand Voyager 2.8 L diesel 2012-2013) treats it as a sign of a failed ignition handshake that new PCM software fixes.
s: No start or delayed start
Check engine light on (Jeep 4xe, Mercedes S 580)
Keyless entry, alarm or key detection not working
c: Engine or security module software mishandles the key handshake (Chrysler, Jeep, Mercedes updates)
Security module without power or ground
Bus line or connector to the security module faulty
Security or keyless entry module faulty

U0169.d: U0169 is set when the sunroof control module drops off the vehicle network. This unit drives the motors for the glass panel and, where fitted, the sun blind, keeps track of their positions and provides the anti-pinch reversal.
s: Sunroof does not open or close electrically
Comfort closing with the key no longer closes the roof
Roof positions or one-touch function lost
c: Sunroof module fuse blown or ground loose
Water at module or connector from blocked roof drains
Headliner wiring or connector to the module damaged

U016A.d: U016A covers the global positioning system module, the receiver that supplies position, speed and time to navigation, telematics and emergency-call functions. Ford uses the code: its 2014 Boss 302S code list includes it, and SSM 54351 explains that 2026 Transit vans built without a telematics control unit may log U016A in the module Ford calls SOBDMC, alongside U0146 in the ABS module.
s: Navigation shows wrong or no position
Telematics or emergency call reports location unavailable
Clock or compass no longer updated by satellite
c: Module not fitted on this build, code without fault (Ford Transit 2026)
GPS or telematics unit without power or ground
Bus wiring or connector at the receiver faulty

U016B.d: U016B appears when the control module of the electric A/C compressor, the inverter fed from the high-voltage battery in hybrids and EVs, stops talking to its partners. In GM's 2016 Volt table (16OBDG01) the engine controller watches frame $222 and fails after 10 s, Type B with MIL after two trips.
s: Air conditioning blows warm
Check engine or service high voltage message, charging possibly limited
Reduced battery cooling or charging power in heat
c: Compressor unplugged while the bus was awake, stored code without real fault (GM 18-NA-096)
Compressor low-voltage harness chafed on axle shaft or bracket (GM PIC6609)
Compressor control module without 12 V supply or ground

U016C.d: U016C concerns fuel pump control module B, the second pump driver in vehicles with two pumps or two tanks; module A has U0109. Ford's 2020-2023 gasoline OBD summary watches pump B through its duty-cycle feedback line: a signal stuck at 0 % or 100 % sets U016C within 2-5 s at 11-16 V.
s: Check engine light on
Crank but no start, or stalling
Lack of power or rough running under load
c: Loose or corroded frame ground at the pump module (Ram G803A)
Fuse or relay for pump B or its driver open
Feedback or bus wiring between pump driver B and PCM damaged
Fuel pump control module B faulty

U016D.d: U016D refers to exhaust gas sensor module B, a second smart sensor unit in the exhaust that heats a probe, evaluates it and reports oxygen or NOx readings as bus data instead of an analog voltage. Module A has U011A.
s: Check engine light on
Readiness monitors for catalyst or exhaust sensors not complete
Diesel: SCR or emission warning, possibly reduced power
c: Sensor module connector or harness damaged by exhaust heat or corrosion
Sensor module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Bus line to the module chafed under the vehicle
Sensor module B or integrated probe electronics faulty

U0170.d: U0170 is the first slot in the J2012 block for remote restraint sensors: sensor A has gone silent for the airbag control unit or another listener. Chrysler follows that scheme.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Early frontal crash detection on the left reduced (Chrysler)
On GM vehicles further U-codes in several modules at the same time
c: Connector at the front satellite sensor unplugged or corroded, often after front-end repairs
Sensor A or its bracket damaged in a frontal knock
On GM vehicles (passenger presence module) chafed or pinched low-speed LAN wiring
Sensor input of the airbag control unit faulty

U0171.d: U0171 says the airbag control unit receives nothing more from restraint sensor B. Chrysler documents it as the up-front right satellite acceleration sensor, the mirror image of U0170, in each Jeep airbag listing it supplied for investigation PE11-019, starting with the 2007 Wrangler; an internal defect of that unit is logged separately as B1B71.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal impact sensing on the right side relies on the central unit only
Code comes back immediately after clearing while the fault persists
c: Connector of the right front sensor not reconnected after bumper or front-end work
Water or road salt in the sensor connector at the front
Front satellite sensor B damaged in a collision
Sensor line to the airbag unit open or shorted

U0172.d: U0172 marks a lost link to restraint sensor C. Chrysler uses it for the first left side satellite acceleration sensor in the Jeep tables of NHTSA file PE11-019.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side and curtain airbag deployment may be impaired
Fault can be intermittent with wet carpets or after rain
c: Water in the left footwell or sill area reaching the sensor connector
Connector disturbed during seat, carpet or trim removal
Left side satellite sensor failed after a side knock
Airbag control unit input or configuration faulty

U0173.d: U0173 tells that the airbag control unit no longer receives data from remote crash sensor D. Such satellite sensors sit in the crumple zone, doors or pillars and report acceleration in one or two axes so the control unit can judge direction and severity of an impact.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact detection on the affected side reduced
Code stays active until the sensor link is restored
c: Loose or corroded connector at satellite sensor D
Sensor line damaged, e.g. in the door or pillar area
Satellite sensor D failed (water ingress, impact)
Sensor input of the airbag control unit faulty

U0174.d: U0174 refers to restraint sensor E, the fifth remote crash sensor in J2012 lettering. No manufacturer documents U0174 publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Scan tool lists sensor E as not responding
Deployment paths depending on sensor E may be blocked
c: Airbag unit coded for a sensor E that is not fitted (e.g. after unit replacement)
Connector at sensor E loose, wet or corroded
Two-wire sensor line open or shorted

U0175.d: U0175 is set when restraint sensor F stops reporting. Chrysler names it the right side satellite acceleration sensor 1 throughout the restraint code lists of the NHTSA probe PE11-019, from the 2007 Wrangler JK to the 2008 Grand Cherokee and Commander; its counterpart on the left is U0172, and B1B75 flags an internal defect of the sensor.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side and curtain airbag readiness reduced
Fault may appear only on bumpy roads (loose contact)
c: Moisture in the right footwell or sill reaching the connector
Connector or line disturbed when the passenger seat was removed
Wrong sensor version or mounting orientation after replacement

U0176.d: U0176 points to restraint sensor G. In Chrysler's usage, as recorded in the NHTSA investigation PE11-019, it is the second right side satellite acceleration sensor.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact detection for the rear right area reduced
Code stays active until sensor link or configuration is corrected
c: Connector behind the rear side or pillar trim loose or damaged
Line to the rear right sensor pinched or chafed
Airbag unit configured for a second side sensor the vehicle does not have

U0177.d: U0177 is stored when crash sensor H, the eighth remote sensor of the restraint system in J2012 lettering, stops reporting to the airbag control unit. Remote acceleration or pressure sensors detect front, side or rear impacts early and feed the central unit that decides on deployment.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Impact detection in the zone of sensor H unavailable
Code returns immediately after clearing
c: Connector at sensor H loose, wet or corroded
Sensor wiring damaged by trim or body work
Airbag control unit input faulty or wrong configuration

U0178.d: U0178 covers restraint sensor I, the ninth remote crash sensor; unlike many letter series, J2012 does use the letter I here. No manufacturer documents U0178 publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Fault may come and go with door movement
Impact detection in the zone of sensor I unavailable
c: Broken wire in the door hinge passage
Water inside the door at the sensor connector (failed vapour barrier)
Sensor interface of the airbag unit faulty

U0179.d: U0179 closes the J2012 block for remote restraint sensors and names sensor J, the tenth position (the letter I is used as well, see U0178). The airbag control unit checks that each connected satellite keeps sending; if sensor J falls silent, the unit stores U0179, switches on the airbag warning lamp and may disable the deployment paths that rely on it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint deployment relying on sensor J may be disabled
Scan tool shows sensor J as not responding
c: Connector at sensor J loose or corroded
Open or shorted line between sensor J and the airbag unit
Crash sensor J failed, e.g. after a minor impact

U017A.d: U017A is logged when restraint sensor K, the eleventh remote crash sensor, has stopped sending data to the restraints module. No manufacturer documents U017A publicly; the Chrysler Jeep lists in NHTSA file PE11-019 end at the sixth satellite.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint functions depending on sensor K may be disabled
Scan tool shows sensor K as absent
c: Sensor K not reconnected after rear-end or boot floor repairs
Sensor line damaged along the rear body
Airbag unit configuration does not match the fitted sensors

U017B.d: U017B means sensor L of the restraint system, the twelfth remote crash sensor in J2012 order, no longer answers. No manufacturer documents U017B publicly, so which component sits behind the letter depends on the car.
s: Airbag or pedestrian protection warning on
Protective function assigned to sensor L disabled
Fault appears after body or bumper work
c: Sensor or its connector not refitted after bumper replacement
Sensor or wiring damaged by a minor front or side knock
Corroded connector in an exposed mounting position

U017C.d: U017C is stored once restraint sensor M, the thirteenth remote crash sensor, falls silent. No manufacturer documents U017C publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on or flickering
Code stored as history after the lamp went out again
Impact detection in the zone of sensor M unavailable while active
c: Intermittent contact at sensor M connector (history code)
Sensor not seated or sealed correctly after trim work

U017D.d: U017D concerns restraint sensor N, the last of the fourteen sensor letters A to N; the two codes that follow belong to seat belt pretensioner modules. No manufacturer documents U017D publicly, and the Chrysler Jeep tables in NHTSA file PE11-019 never go past G.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Scan tool reports no response from sensor N
Restraint deployment relying on sensor N may be disabled
c: Connector at sensor N loose or corroded
Earlier wiring repair untwisted or with unsuitable connectors
Airbag unit expects a sensor N that is not installed

U017E.d: U017E reports that seat belt pretensioner module A no longer communicates. Such modules drive electric, reversible belt tensioners: Audi pre sense pulls the front belts tight by small motors when it senses emergency braking or skidding and releases them if no crash follows.
s: Warning message for pre-crash occupant protection
Belt no longer pre-tightened during emergency braking
Airbag lamp on; on some FCA models MIL as well
c: Connector at the belt retractor module in the pillar loose or damaged
New retractor with control module not coded or basic setting not done
Harness damaged or wrongly routed (Jeep JL, shifter area)
Software issue in the module or a listener such as the PCM (FCA 2021)

U017F.d: U017F is the second pretensioner module code: module B has dropped off its link to the airbag unit. Audi documents it together with U017E00 in bulletin 2081251 for 2025-26 A5, A6, Q5 and Q6 e-tron models, where both codes accompany a proactive occupant protection warning and dealers are asked to file a case report.
s: Pre-crash protection fault message in the instrument cluster
Reversible belt tightening on one seat inoperative
Often stored together with U017E
c: Retractor with control module replaced but not coded or basic-set
Supply or bus connector at module B loose
Bus line between airbag unit and module B damaged

U0180.d: U0180 belongs to the automatic lighting control module, the unit that evaluates a light sensor and switches the headlamps on at dusk, in tunnels or with the wipers. Once it is silent, the auto-light feature can no longer be commanded.
s: Automatic headlamps no longer switch on or off
Headlamps stay on as a default
GM Cadillac: no audio, chimes or turn-signal sound
c: Light sensor or lighting module without power or ground
Moisture at connectors after rain or car wash (GM PIE0348)
Bus or LIN line to the windscreen sensor damaged

U0181.d: U0181 says the module that controls automatic headlamp levelling has dropped off the bus. That module reads ride-height sensors on the axles and drives the actuator motors in the headlamps to keep the beam at the right angle under load.
s: Headlamp beam height no longer adjusts
Headlamp or lighting warning in the cluster
Oncoming traffic dazzled or road poorly lit when loaded
c: Levelling module without power or ground
Chafed harness or water in connectors or BCM area (GM Acadia/XT5)
Corroded connector at the module near the headlamp
Headlamp levelling module faulty or not coded

U0182.d: U0182 is logged when the front lighting control module stops talking on the bus. This module drives front lamp functions such as swivelling or adaptive beam patterns.
s: Adaptive or cornering light inoperative
Lighting warning lamp or message in the cluster
Front lamps fall back to a fixed default beam
c: Front lighting module without power or ground
Corroded connector in the engine bay or headlamp area
Bus line to the module chafed or open

U0183.d: U0183 refers to rear lighting control module A, the unit that drives tail, brake, turn and in some designs reversing lamps at the back of the vehicle. A second rear unit, B, has U0252, the front module U0182.
s: Tail, brake or turn lamps at the rear not working
Bulb or lighting warning in the cluster
Rear lamps in a fixed default mode
