c: Rear lighting module without power or ground
Wiring broken in the tailgate or boot lid hinge loom
Corroded connector at the rear lamp or module
Rear lighting control module A faulty

U0184.d: U0184 is logged when the radio or infotainment head unit no longer answers on the bus; cluster, gateway, HVAC or amplifier store it, often several at once. GM bulletin 16-NA-115 (many 2014 GM models) reprograms the radio when it stays silent, shows a dark display or fails to wake up.
s: Radio dead, screen blank or no sound
Phone, reversing camera or voice control not available
U0184 stored in several modules
c: Radio software hang or wake-up problem, fixed by reset or reprogramming (GM, Ford)
Spread or pushed-out terminals at radio or security gateway (Stellantis)

U0185.d: U0185 indicates that the antenna control module has stopped communicating. This unit, frequently an amplifier or tuner box near the rear screen, the roof fin or a bumper, conditions radio, TV, satellite or GPS signals and in some designs raises or lowers a motorised mast.
s: Poor or no radio reception
Satellite, TV or GPS reception lost
Power antenna does not move
c: Antenna module without power or ground
Water ingress at roof fin or rear-screen amplifier
Bus wiring or connector to the antenna unit damaged

U0186.d: U0186 means the external audio amplifier A has dropped off the bus; the radio or cluster store it, and the speakers usually go quiet. GM PIC6153 (Volt 2016 with premium audio) warns against replacing the amplifier and asks to inspect its X1 connector, especially pin 4 (B+) and pin 8 (ground).
s: No sound or radio muted
Crackling or intermittent audio
Chimes or warning tones missing
c: Spread or backed-out terminals at amplifier or head unit connector (GM, Mazda)
Amplifier software stops bus communication, fixed by flash (Chrysler)
Amplifier fuse blown or ground loose

U0187.d: U0187 opens the J2012 series for networked disc players and changers: module A is the main CD or DVD drive, while U0188 to U0190 cover B to D. In many older cars the changer sat apart from the head unit, in the glovebox, under a seat or in the trunk, and reported to it over a data line.
s: CD or DVD source missing or not selectable
Disc cannot be loaded or ejected
Other audio sources work normally
c: Disc unit A without power or ground
Data line or connector to the changer (glovebox, seat, trunk) damaged
Drive removed or head unit coded for a drive not fitted

U0188.d: U0188 means the second networked disc player or changer, module B, no longer answers. Disc changers hold several CDs or DVDs and were often mounted apart from the radio, in the dash, a console or the boot, and linked to the infotainment bus.
s: Disc source B missing or not selectable
Discs not ejected or not played
Code stored in the radio or head unit
c: Disc unit B without power or ground
Bus or connector to the changer (often in boot or console) damaged
Unit removed or vehicle coded for a device not fitted

U0189.d: U0189 covers the third disc player or changer on the bus, module C. Systems with more than one drive are found mostly in rear-seat entertainment or luxury setups, where a front unit and separate rear players feed different screens.
s: Rear or third disc source unavailable
Rear screen shows no disc content
Code stored in the head unit
c: Disc unit C fuse blown or ground loose
Connector or bus wiring to the rear player damaged
Vehicle coded for a third drive that is not fitted

U018A.d: U018A covers headlamp leveling control module B. Cars with separate levelling electronics in each headlamp, or with a central controller plus lamp-side units, need a second address; U0181 is the first module.
s: One headlamp no longer adjusts its beam height
Headlamp or lighting warning in the cluster
Uneven or very low beam pattern
c: Levelling module B without power or ground
Corroded connector at the headlamp from moisture
Bus line to the headlamp damaged after a front-end repair
Headlamp levelling module B faulty or not coded

U0190.d: U0190 is the last code in the J2012 disc player block and names module D, a fourth networked drive or changer. When that unit goes silent, the modules expecting its periodic traffic store U0190; GM's procedure for U0100-U02FF adds that a code stored only in history after a flat battery or a module disconnected with the bus awake is not a reason to replace parts.
s: Disc source D missing
Magazine not loaded or ejected
Code stored in the head unit
c: Disc unit D without power or ground
History entry after flat battery or unit unplugged with bus awake
Connector or bus line to module D damaged

U0191.d: U0191 means the television tuner has dropped off the vehicle network. J2012 simply calls it Television: a receiver for mostly digital terrestrial TV that hands the picture to the central display or to rear screens.
s: TV source missing from the media menu
Black screen or no-signal message when TV is selected
Code stored in radio or display unit
c: TV tuner without power or ground (fuse, connector)
History entry after flat battery or tuner unplugged with bus awake
Bus line or connector to the tuner damaged

U0192.d: U0192 is reserved for a personal computer that exchanges data with the vehicle network, for example a built-in carputer, a docked laptop in a police or service vehicle, or a PC-based infotainment unit. When that node stops sending, a listening module stores the code.
s: PC functions or data no longer available in the vehicle
Code stored without any noticeable fault
c: Network coding expects a PC that is not fitted or was removed
Retrofit interface, dock or bus connector to the PC faulty
PC or its interface without supply, or shut down
Onboard PC faulty or software hung

U0193.d: U0193 reports that digital audio control module A no longer sends its messages. Makers fill this slot differently.
s: Digital, satellite radio or traffic data unavailable
Radio shows no signal for the digital source
Code stored in radio and other modules
c: Digital receiver module without power or ground
Chafed harness or water in connectors (GM Acadia/XT5)
Bus wire or connector to the receiver damaged

U0194.d: U0194 marks the second digital audio control module, B, as silent on the bus. GM uses the code but does not name the module publicly: on the 2013-2014 Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia the radio stores U0194 together with many other U-codes when the harness of the rear side object detection sensors rubs on the exhaust and disturbs the network.
s: Radio shuts off or audio source drops out intermittently
Many U-codes stored at the same time
Cluster or other modules act up together with the radio
c: Network harness chafed elsewhere in the car disturbing the bus (GM Lambda)
Water in a bus connector (Ford C-MAX)
Audio module B without power or ground

U0195.d: U0195 concerns the subscription entertainment receiver module, the box that decodes a paid broadcast service such as SiriusXM satellite radio. Earlier code lists named it Satellite Radio Receiver Module, and makers have used it in that sense: Chrysler's code list for 2006-2010 Jeep models, filed with NHTSA in a defect investigation, reads U0195 as Lost Communication With SDARS, the satellite digital audio receiver.
s: Satellite radio band missing or showing no signal
Subscription service cannot be activated
Code stored in the radio or gateway
c: History entry after low battery voltage or jump start
Bus line or connector to the receiver damaged or corroded

U0196.d: U0196 refers to rear entertainment control module A, the unit that gives rear passengers their own audio or video source, headphone zones and screen control. GM's Saab U-code lists assign it to the rear audio control module for the 9-5 (2010-2011) and the 9-4X (2011), meaning the rear audio panel with headphone sockets.
s: Rear audio controls or headphone sockets dead
Rear screens dark or no source selectable
Code stored in radio or gateway
c: Rear entertainment unit without power or ground
Bus wiring to the rear unit pinched or connector loose (seat, console, headliner)
History entry after low battery voltage

U0197.d: U0197 says the telephone control module, in most cars the Bluetooth hands-free unit, has gone quiet on the bus. FCA uses it widely under the name Hands Free Phone Module.
s: Phone does not pair or calls are not possible hands-free
Display reports the hands-free module is still loading
MIL on in some FCA models
c: Hands-free module software hangs at boot (FCA update)
Bus line or connector to the phone module faulty

U0198.d: U0198 marks the telematic control module as silent; that unit holds the cellular modem for remote apps, emergency and assistance calls. Ford's APIM stores it on 2012-2018 Focus Electric, Fusion Energi and C-MAX Energi when the TCU hangs: SSM 46534 and 47198 report a drained battery, dead MyFord Mobile features and no modem ESN, cured by pulling the TCU fuse for five minutes and reprogramming.
s: Remote app, emergency or assistance call unavailable
Battery drained overnight (Ford plug-in models)
Network warning in the cluster, often with further U-codes
c: Telematics unit hung or outdated software (Ford TCU reprogramming)
Water or corrosion in a body harness connector (GM X901)
Low-speed bus wire pinched or chafed in the roof or body
False history entry from a module self-test (Ford Super Duty)

U0199.d: U0199 reports that door control module A has dropped off the bus; most makers assign it to the driver's door. Chrysler bulletin 08-061-12 (300 and Charger 2005-2010) calls it the driver door module: the front windows and central locking stop working, a one-minute battery disconnect is tried first, and the module is replaced if contact does not return.
s: Power windows and locks on the door inoperative
Windows move on their own or several warning lamps light up
Mirror adjustment or switch lighting dead
c: Loose or backed-out pins in the door-to-body connector (VW)
Broken wires in the door hinge harness

U019A.d: U019A is stored when the tachograph stops sending on the vehicle bus. Tachographs log speed, distance and driving time in trucks and buses; in the EU every newly registered vehicle of that class has needed a digital unit since May 2006.
s: Tachograph warning or speed display missing
Cruise control or road speed limiter unavailable
Code stored in the engine controller
c: Tachograph without power, ground or ignition signal
CAN wiring or connector behind the tachograph damaged
Tachograph replaced or recalibrated without matching the bus configuration

U019B.d: U019B means battery charger control module A, the on-board charger of a plug-in vehicle, is no longer heard on the bus. Ford's 2014 OBD code list flags U019B as MIL-relevant, in line with CARB's rule that plug-in hybrids must detect charger faults that stop or slow charging.
s: Vehicle does not charge or charge plug stays locked
Electrical system warning, drive system cannot be activated
Export power or backup power features unavailable
c: Damaged wires at harness couplings exposed to the environment (Audi A7 PHEV)
Gateway or controller software (Ford Lightning, Audi e-tron GT)
Charger without 12 V supply, ground or wake-up signal

U019C.d: U019C points to a second glow plug control module, needed where a diesel has more preheating channels than one unit drives, for example one module per cylinder bank. No manufacturer documents U019C publicly; it is absent from GM's diesel tables and from the NHTSA bulletin index.
s: Hard starting when cold
White smoke and rough idle until warm
Preheat lamp behaves oddly, MIL on
c: Glow plug module 2 without supply, ground or ignition feed
Water or corrosion in the module connector near the engine
Bus line to module 2 chafed or connector loose

U019D.d: U019D concerns a temperature sensor at a direct ozone reduction (DOR) catalyst that reports over the network rather than a plain wire; the wired versions have P2567-P2571. A DOR catalyst is a coating on the radiator or A/C condenser that turns ozone in the passing air into oxygen, such as Engelhard's PremAir, first fitted by Volvo on the S80 and by Nissan on the Sentra CA.
s: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
DOR monitor shown as not complete
c: Sensor connector at the radiator corroded or damaged by road debris
Sensor left unplugged or radiator replaced after front-end repair
Bus or supply line to the sensor broken

U019E.d: U019E covers the transmission range control module, in shift-by-wire designs the electronics that engage park, reverse, neutral or drive on behalf of the driver's selector. Ford lists U019E in its 2014 OBD code list without the MIL marker it gives emissions-related codes.
s: Gear selection refused or vehicle stays in park
Shift system warning in the cluster
Transmission engages park on its own when stopping
c: Range control module without power, ground or wake-up
Bus connector at the transmission corroded or loose
Low battery voltage during cranking or parking

U019F.d: U019F means the electric engine coolant pump, which carries its own control electronics, has stopped answering. Mercedes documents it on two engines: on the M256 six-cylinder the engine controller stores U019F00 or U019F87 with a red coolant warning; LI20.10-P-075374 checks the 12 V and 48 V plugs of pump M75/11, its ground and fuse F153/2 and, if the pump touches the heat shield, insulates it or replaces the control
s: Red coolant temperature warning
MIL or check engine lamp on
Engine power reduced to protect against overheating
c: Pump supply plug, 48 V connector or ground loose or dirty (Mercedes)
Water or corrosion in front-end connectors (Ford hybrids)
Similar-looking pumps swapped or wrong part ordered (Mazda PHEV)

U01A0.d: U01A0 names battery interface control module A, the first slave board that reports cell voltages and temperatures of its pack section to the battery controller. GM's 2016-2019 plug-in hybrid tables explain how the code arises: the battery system module talks to eight such boards over a UART daisy chain; once U179C shows that data has stopped, it switches the boards into an internal loopback test and stores the code o
s: Vehicle does not become ready to drive, red hybrid/EV warning
MIL on after the first failing trip (GM Type A)
Further module codes or U179C stored at the same time
c: Chain wiring or connector between battery controller and module A interrupted
Module A without supply from its cell group or low-voltage feed
Battery interface control module A defective
Chain interface of the battery controller itself faulty

U01A1.d: U01A1 refers to battery interface control module B. In GM's eAssist mild hybrids it is the second and final board: bulletin PIT5513D lists two high-voltage battery interface control modules, K112A and K112B, for Silverado and Sierra trucks of 2016 to 2018 and the 2018 LaCrosse, and the GM tables 16OBDG07B and 19OBDG03B accordingly contain only U01A0 and U01A1.
s: MIL only after two consecutive failing trips (GM Type B)
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid system warning message
c: Chain connection between module A and module B interrupted or corroded
Battery interface control module B (GM K112B) defective
Common low-voltage feed of the powerpack interrupted (then usually A as well)

U01A2.d: U01A2 is stored when battery interface control module C, the third board of the chain, stays silent. How a controller reaches that verdict is spelled out in GM's 2016 hybrid table: the battery system module first logs U179C for one or more missing boards, then orders all boards into a loopback mode that bypasses the daisy chain.
s: Electrical system or hybrid warning in the instrument cluster
Reduced drive power or no electric driving
Code returns immediately after clearing
c: Chain link between module B and module C broken (connector, ribbon, pin)
Module C fails the loopback test, board defective
Battery controller software that misreads the chain (update available)

U01A3.d: U01A3 marks a lost link to battery interface control module D. Before this generic block existed, GM used proprietary numbers for the same fault: the GM U-code list published for the 2011 Saab 9-4X names U2603 to U2606 as the battery energy control module losing hybrid battery interface modules 1 to 4.
s: MIL and hybrid/EV warning (GM Type A)
Limited power, electric range shortened
Cell voltages of one pack section shown as unavailable
c: Chain connection from module C to module D interrupted
Battery interface control module D defective
Scan tool or software generation reports the board under the older GM number

U01A4.d: U01A4 concerns battery interface control module E. Whether such a code points to one board or to a whole broken chain depends on the wiring scheme.
s: Battery warning and reduced output
Only module E reported missing although later boards are silent too (open chain)
MIL on the first trip (GM Type A)
c: Chain link between module D and module E interrupted (open chain)
Module E itself defective (likely in ring designs when neighbours still report)
Return path of a ring layout damaged in addition to the main path

U01A5.d: U01A5 says the battery controller no longer receives data from interface module F. Once such a board drops out, the cells it covers are unsupervised: no voltage readings, no temperatures and no balancing for that section.
s: Drive system cannot be activated, red warning lamp
Charging refused or stopped early
Other battery diagnostics suspended while the code is active
c: Chain connection between module E and module F interrupted
Battery interface control module F defective
Board F loses supply because its cell group or sense tap is open

U01A6.d: U01A6 means battery interface control module G no longer reports to the battery controller. Because these boards sit inside the high-voltage pack, the chain runs between modules whose ground levels differ by hundreds of volts, so the link has to be galvanically isolated; Wikipedia's battery management article names optical couplers and radio as the hardware routes.
s: MIL and battery warning lamp
Insulation fault code stored alongside if moisture has entered
Reduced power or no ready mode
c: Moisture or coolant at the chain connectors of module G
Chain link between module F and module G interrupted
Isolating coupler (transformer, optocoupler) on the link to G failed
Battery interface control module G defective

U01A7.d: U01A7 refers to battery interface control module H. On packs with exactly eight boards it is the tail of the chain: the GM plug-in hybrid tables for 2016 to 2019 stop at U01A7, and both Audi bulletins (A3 Sportback e-tron 2016, Q5 e 2022 and 2024) list precisely U01A000 to U01A700.
s: MIL on the first trip (GM Type A)
Electrical system or hybrid warning, power reduced
All other module letters report normally
c: Final chain link from module G to module H interrupted
Battery interface control module H defective
Termination or return line at the end of the chain faulty

U01A8.d: U01A8 is the code for battery interface control module I and is only needed on packs with more than eight monitoring boards. GM's 2018 hybrid table contains it solely inside the fault bundle BICM Loss of Comm (U01A0-U01AC), adding that GM shares software across programs and only codes valid for the vehicle at hand apply; there is no monitor entry of its own, so neither threshold nor MIL type is published for I.
s: Battery or hybrid warning, power limited
Charging blocked
c: Chain connection between module H and module I interrupted
Battery interface control module I defective
Battery controller configured for more boards than fitted

U01A9.d: U01A9 stands for battery interface control module J, the tenth board. Apart from wiring, a typical trigger after repairs is configuration: monitoring chips in a chain usually get their address when communication starts.
s: Code appears right after battery repair or module replacement
Vehicle not ready to drive or power limited
c: Board J not addressed or registered after module replacement
Chain connection between module I and module J interrupted
Battery interface control module J defective

U01AA.d: U01AA covers battery interface control module K, the eleventh board, so only large packs can set it at all. Not every design uses wires for this link: GM's Ultium platform monitors its cells by radio, a system developed with Analog Devices, which according to Wikipedia needs about 90 % less wiring.
s: Battery warning, reduced range and power
DC fast charging limited or refused
c: Wired link to K interrupted or, in wireless systems, radio link lost
Replacement board K not registered with the battery controller
Battery interface control module K defective

U01AB.d: U01AB points at battery interface control module L, the twelfth position. The link to such a board has to bridge a large voltage offset, because the lowest and highest boards of a stack sit hundreds of volts apart.
s: Battery or hybrid warning
Power limited, charging may be blocked
c: Isolating transformer or capacitor on the link to L failed
Twisted-pair chain line to module L chafed, pinched or unplugged
Battery interface control module L defective

U01AC.d: U01AC belongs to battery interface control module M and is the last one GM mentions: its 2018 hybrid table ends the fault bundle BICM Loss of Comm at U01AC, i.e. thirteen boards, whereas GM's model-specific tables from 2016 to 2019 only monitor A to H.
s: Summary code for missing boards stored together with U01AC
Battery warning and reduced output
c: Chain connection between module L and module M interrupted
Battery interface control module M defective
Controller calibration expects more boards than the pack contains

U01AD.d: U01AD names battery interface control module N, the fourteenth board in a monitoring chain. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and even GM's broad fault bundle stops at M.
s: Battery warning, power and charging limited
Cell data of one pack section missing in the scan tool
c: Chain connection between module M and module N interrupted
Battery interface control module N defective

U01AE.d: U01AE concerns battery interface control module O, which only exists in systems with at least fifteen monitoring nodes; no manufacturer documents the code publicly. Wikipedia distinguishes three ways to organise battery management: centralised (one controller wired to every cell), modular (several controllers, each covering a group of cells) and distributed (a board per cell with a single communication cable).
s: Warning lamp, power reduced
Charging postponed or refused
c: Internal link to module O interrupted
Battery interface control module O defective
Board O without supply from its cell group

U01AF.d: U01AF closes the row and stands for battery interface control module P, the sixteenth monitoring board; no manufacturer documents it publicly. Some packs exceed that count: according to Wikipedia the Hummer EV battery consists of 24 Ultium modules, although that platform monitors wirelessly and GM does not publish how it maps modules to codes.
s: Battery warning while the battery controller itself still communicates
Power limited, charging blocked
c: Internal link to module P interrupted
Battery interface control module P defective

U01B0.d: U01B0 says the 12 V battery monitor module, a small sensor on the negative battery post that reports voltage, current, temperature and state of charge, has stopped replying. GM polls it over LIN: its 2018 engine tables (18OBDG03A) flag the code once frame 18_C02 has been absent for 1.25 s, the 2025 body controller tables (25OBDG04A) after 12.6 s; both rate it Type B, two trips.
s: Stop/start system disabled, message in the driver display
MIL on
Battery state of charge shown wrongly or battery saver functions inactive
c: Loose, corroded or damaged LIN connector or wire at the battery sensor
Weak or deeply discharged 12 V battery
Battery monitor sensor faulty (GM replaces it after the checks)
Parasitic drain preventing the sensor relearn

U01B1.d: U01B1 concerns a second particulate matter sensor in a diesel exhaust, used where a layout needs two of them. Such smart sensors carry their own control unit, which heats the element, measures soot build-up and sends the results to the engine controller over CAN.
s: MIL on
Particulate filter monitor shows as not complete
c: Heat-damaged or corroded harness or connector at sensor B near the exhaust
Sensor control unit without supply voltage or ground (fuse, relay)
Control unit of PM sensor B faulty

U01B2.d: Hybrid transmissions such as the two-mode system developed by GM, Daimler, Chrysler and BMW use two or three planetary gear sets plus clutches to switch between power-split and fixed-ratio operation. A planetary gear set control module would run those shift elements and report their state to the hybrid or transmission controller.
s: Hybrid system warning
Reduced power or limited fallback mode
MIL on
c: Damaged CAN wiring or connector at the transmission
Module without supply voltage or ground
Planetary gear set control module faulty

U01B3.d: The brake blending actuator divides each braking request between regeneration by the drive motor and the friction brakes, keeping pedal feel steady while the share shifts. Bosch states that its electromechanical iBooster, together with the ESP hev unit, can blend up to 0.3 g of deceleration.
s: Little or no regenerative braking
Changed brake pedal feel
Brake or hybrid system warning
c: CAN wiring or connector fault at the brake actuator
Actuator without supply voltage, often after low 12 V voltage

U01B4.d: Brake system control module B is the second brake controller in a two-unit layout, often the electric brake booster beside the stability control unit. GM's 2018 table for the CT6 plug-in hybrid (18OBDG01) has the engine controller flag U01B4 when frame $4FB from BSC2 has been missing for 10 s on the high-speed bus, Type B, two trips.
s: MIL on, sometimes with brake or stability warnings
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Changed brake pedal feel if the booster is affected
c: Booster run-on interrupted at switch-off (Porsche, no part fault)
Damaged CAN wiring or connector at the brake module
Low 12 V supply during start or shutdown
Brake system control module B faulty

U01B5.d: Electric catalyst heating lets the converter start working within seconds of a cold start. Emitec's EMICAT disc runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to 300 A; in high-voltage hybrids Vitesco feeds it through a dedicated DC/DC converter, one form of the separate power electronics that make up a catalyst heater control module.
s: MIL on
Higher emissions and possibly rough running after a cold start
c: Heat or corrosion damage at the heater module connectors near the exhaust
Module supply or high-current fuse open

U01B6.d: A fuel heater warms diesel ahead of the filter so that paraffin wax, which separates out in the cold, cannot clog the element; ordinary diesel turns to gel at roughly −15 to −19 °C. Newer designs use a microcontroller: a patent describes a heater controller that sets power from outside air temperature in open loop or from fuel temperature in closed loop, and cuts out when battery voltage falls too low.
s: Hard starting or stalling in frost
Power loss from a clogged fuel filter in cold weather
Often no symptom in mild weather
c: Corroded or loose connector at the filter housing heater
Heater module supply fuse or relay failed

U01B7.d: A switch input module collects a group of buttons, for instance in a door trim, steering wheel or centre console, and sends their states to other units as network messages instead of wiring every switch on its own. A patent by Eaton describes the idea: a central unit queries every switch by its address and accepts only answers whose address and state are valid.
s: A group of buttons without function
Switch backlight or indicator lamps dark
c: Loose connector or broken wire at the switch panel
Liquid spilled into the switch module

U01B8.d: Carmakers that fit more than one switch input module count them A, B, C. A modular layout patented by BCS Automotive Interface Solutions shows why there can be several: a main switch module, for example for the lighting, is extended by satellite modules of different kinds, and coding contacts in the connectors tell the main unit which type is plugged in.
s: Buttons served by module B without function
Other switch groups still working
c: Connector of module B unplugged, loose or corroded
Missing supply voltage or ground at module B

U01B9.d: Module C is the third switch input module. Such units often hang off a sub-bus: a Yazaki patent on door electronics shows a door unit that takes commands from CAN and forwards them over a LIN sub-bus to local nodes such as switches, window lift and mirror.
s: Buttons served by module C ignored
Fault appears or disappears when moving a door, seat or the steering wheel
c: Wire broken in a moving harness section (door hinge, seat rail, steering column)
Fault in the unit that hosts the sub-bus of module C

U01BA.d: With park-by-wire, an electric actuator drives the parking pawl into a toothed wheel on the transmission output; no cable links it to the selector, so the park lock module alone decides when the pawl may drop in, normally only at standstill because at speed it would just ratchet over the teeth. U01BA is set when the transmission or vehicle controller loses contact with this module.
s: Vehicle will not shift out of Park or Park not confirmed
Warning to secure the vehicle with the parking brake
c: Connector or wiring fault at the park lock actuator on the transmission
Low 12 V supply, e.g. weak battery

U01BB.d: Battery charger control module B is, by its name, a second on-board charger, as fitted on some electric cars to raise AC charging power. Polestar uses the code differently: Technical Journal 37630 (2026, vehicle type 359 from model year 2025) lists U01BB00 in the central computer GCCC when its only AC charger, the grid-to-HV converter GHCA, has failed.
s: AC charging impossible while DC fast charging works
Charging fault message or charge port LED error
c: On-board charger unit failed (Polestar GHCA replaced)
Charger without 12 V supply, ground or wake-up signal
Bus wiring or connector at the charger damaged

U01BC.d: Engines with a water-cooled charge air cooler run a separate low-temperature coolant loop with an electric pump, usually a LIN slave of the engine controller. Rheinmetall's pumps of this kind are driven via PWM or LIN, and Bosch's PCE pump has a built-in diagnostic function reported to a higher-level unit.
s: MIL on
Reduced power or boost, especially in hot weather
c: Water or corrosion in the pump connector at the front of the engine bay
Pump supply fuse or relay open
Electric coolant pump B electronics or motor faulty

U01BD.d: Electrified cars may carry several DC/DC converters, each turning one direct voltage into another: the main unit supplies the 12 V system from the traction battery, others feed 48 V consumers or single heavy loads. Vitesco, for instance, added a dedicated DC/DC converter in high-voltage hybrids purely to power the electrically heated catalyst.
s: Electrical system or 12 V warning
Comfort loads switched off to save energy
c: Low-voltage supply, wake-up line or connector of converter C faulty
Converter shut down by an open high-voltage interlock or contactor state
DC/DC converter C control electronics faulty

U01BE.d: Some electrified drivetrains can uncouple a drive motor from its wheels so that an idle motor is not spun by the road. The Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray has such a disconnect: GM bulletin 24-NA-273 (January 2025, 2024–2025 models with LT2 engine) ties U01BE with a lit MIL to an internal microchip fault in the M162 drive motor disconnect clutch actuator, and the remedy is a new actuator.
s: MIL on
Electric drive on one axle or all-wheel drive unavailable
Reduced acceleration
c: Internal electronic fault in the clutch actuator (GM M162 replaced)
Connector or wiring fault at the actuator on the drive unit
Actuator without supply voltage or ground

U01BF.d: A battery management control module watches cell voltages, temperatures and current and decides how much power a pack may deliver or accept. The J2012 name does not tie it to the high-voltage battery.
s: Battery or electrical system warning
Charging or drive power limited
MIL on (GM Type B)
c: Bus wiring or connector between gateway and battery module damaged
Module supply interrupted or 12 V voltage too low
